sketches.title: The Dare Ladder
sketches.premise: You and a friend are building one ridiculous dare, rung by rung. Start with a harmless dare, then take turns adding exactly one harder rule while keeping every earlier rule; if your rung breaks the ladder, you lose suddenly.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds one doable escalation to the same dare, keeps every earlier rule, and leaves a clear next step; a skipped link jumps difficulty without a bridge, an ending makes the dare complete with no next rung, and an undo removes or weakens a standing rule.
sketches.move_shape: Add one rule that makes the same dare harder, not a new dare. Example: “Do the dare while wearing oven mitts.” The host says, “That rung holds: it keeps the dare and adds one obstacle.”
sketches.first_card: Dare someone to carry a spoon across the room.

sketches.title: The Tiny Quest
sketches.premise: You are guiding a toy-sized hero through one shared adventure, one small action at a time. Each turn must move the same quest forward while honoring every fact already established; the best moves make the hero's troubles funny, not impossible.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it is the next physical step in the stated quest, uses the whole transcript, and changes the hero's situation; a skipped link leaps past needed action, an ending finishes the quest, and an undo cancels an established action or fact.
sketches.move_shape: Add exactly one action by the hero or the world. Example: “The hero climbs onto the spoon.” The host says, “That step holds: the spoon is still there, and the climb gives us a place to go next.”
sketches.first_card: A button is a boat, and the hero must cross the carpet.

sketches.title: Recipe Rumble
sketches.premise: Together you are inventing one strange but edible recipe, adding one step at a time. Keep the same dish and all its ingredients in mind; a safe step may hold, but a clever change that makes your partner handle an odd ingredient scores more.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it is the next cooking step for the same dish, uses or preserves everything already named, and leaves the recipe possible; a skipped link uses an ingredient without preparing or adding it, an ending serves the dish, and an undo removes or reverses a completed cooking step.
sketches.move_shape: Add one cooking action. Example: “Stir the mashed banana into the warm oats.” The host says, “That step holds: both ingredients are present, and the bowl is not served yet.”
sketches.first_card: Make a snack from an apple, crackers, and honey.

sketches.title: Costume Cascade
sketches.premise: You are dressing one person for one increasingly silly event. Take turns adding exactly one wearable item or change, keeping the outfit and event consistent; points favor choices that make your partner explain, balance, or proudly display something goofy.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds one wearable change to the same outfit, fits the event and every item already named, and keeps the person able to wear it; a skipped link replaces the outfit's plan, an ending declares the costume ready, and an undo takes off or negates an established item.
sketches.move_shape: Add one item or adjustment. Example: “Put a paper crown over the bike helmet.” The host says, “That holds: both head pieces remain, and the outfit is still being built.”
sketches.first_card: Dress one person to attend a rainy-day parade.

sketches.title: Gift-Wrap Trouble
sketches.premise: You are wrapping one present together, making the job harder with each turn without losing track of what the gift and package are. Each move adds one real wrapping step or a harmless complication, and the funniest cost is what your partner must now manage.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it is the next step in wrapping the same present, respects the package's current state and materials, and keeps wrapping possible; a skipped link uses a finished result before making it, an ending seals and labels the gift, and an undo tears back or removes a standing wrapping step.
sketches.move_shape: Add one wrapping action or complication. Example: “Fold the paper around the box but leave the corners open.” The host says, “That holds: the box is partly covered, so the next turn has corners to solve.”
sketches.first_card: Wrap a small book using one sheet of paper and a ribbon.

sketches.title: Museum Mission
sketches.premise: You and a partner are carrying out one careful museum mission, adding exactly one action at a time. The mission may become trickier, but every move must preserve the goal, the location, and the objects already in play; points reward the extra care your move makes your partner take.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it is the next action toward the same museum goal, fits the whole scene and its rules, and leaves the mission unfinished; a skipped link jumps over a necessary action, an ending completes the mission, and an undo cancels an action or returns an object to an earlier stated place.
sketches.move_shape: Add one mission action. Example: “Ask the guard which case holds the blue coin.” The host says, “That holds: the goal remains, the guard is in the scene, and the answer gives us a next move.”
sketches.first_card: Find the missing label for a dinosaur bone before the museum closes.
